newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION - SMALL AND MULDER OUT OF DURBAN TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - SMALL AND MULDER OUT OF DURBAN TEST.

text.p: The Springbok back line was further depleted on Tuesday when winger James Small and centre Japie Mulder both pulled out of Saturday's second test against the British Lions because of injury.
Their withdrawal came only a day after Mulder's fellow centre Edrich Lubbe was ruled out of the last two tests because of a pulled hamstring.
The Lions won the opening test in the three-match series 25-16 in Cape Town on Saturday.
The strong-running Mulder has a pinched nerve in his left shoulder while Small has an injured hamstring.

"Japie's specialist in Johannesburg says there is a lot of bad bruising in his shoulder but that it seems he should be fit enough for consideration for the third test at Ellis Park," South African media liaison officer Herman Coetzee said.
Coetzee said Springbok coach Carel du Plessis had added Western Province wing Pieter Rossouw to his squad in Durban and that one more player would be named to cover for Lubbe.
Rossouw is likely to replace Small on the right wing for the Durban test while Northern Transvaal centre Danie van Schalkwyk is expected to come into the squad for Lubbe.
Coetzee said former Springbok centre Hennie le Roux had not been considered as a replacement because of a groin strain.
The team for Saturday's second test is to be announced on Wednesday.
